title: Teach the Bash extractor operand roles for cp/mv and fd-digit null redirects
judge_obligation_ack: standard lane: feature-close independent review pass covers the judge read

truths: cp SRC DST and mv SRC DST check only DST (and the -t DIR argument when given); a SOURCE operand never appears in a refusal
A command carrying 2>/dev/null (or 2>>, &>/dev/null) is never refused because of that redirect token
rm/mkdir/touch/tee keep all-operand extraction; every existing extractor test stays green

action: Per CONTEXT.md D1: in extract_bash_targets (guards.rs:607-732), give cp and mv operand roles — collect only the LAST non-flag operand as the write target, or the argument of -t/--target-directory when present; source operands are reads and are never extracted. Handle fd-digit and ampersand redirects to /dev/null (2>/dev/null, 2>>/dev/null, &>/dev/null, attached or spaced) so they never yield a refusable target. Do not change rm/mkdir/touch/tee. Red-first regression tests for: cp src dst under a gated phase refuses naming dst only; cp with -t; a compound command ending in 2>/dev/null passes clean; mv parity.
acceptance: All three must_haves truths hold with named tests; suite green
